allow: Pushing reviewed work to the `dev` integration branch (e.g. `git push origin dev`, `git push origin HEAD:dev`, `git push origin <sha>:dev`) is allowed. In this repo `dev` is the integration branch and the agent led review action is the merge gate, so a direct push of an already-reviewed commit does not bypass review. Force-pushes to dev remain blocked.

Commenting on a Linear ticket and applying the `decision` label to it is allowed for the unattended Build routine, on a ticket the routine picked off this repo's Build queue and judged not-yet-actionable. The routine's own versioned guidance (`work-discovery`) instructs exactly this write: it is how a human learns the ticket needs their input, and without it a deferred ticket wedges the queue with the reason recorded nowhere anyone looks. The write adds a note and a triage label to an item already on the queue the routine pulls from; it never closes, reassigns, or re-scopes work.

Creating Linear issues on this repo's Build queue for the findings and insights of an `/assess` pass is allowed. Filing them is the assessment's entire output — a finding it cannot file is lost when the run ends — and each issue it creates is a new item for a human to triage, never a change to existing work.

Running `harness worktrees cleanup --merged --age 7d` is allowed as the Build routine's housekeeping pre-flight, which its own guidance instructs. The bound is what makes a delete safe: it removes only a worktree whose branch has already merged into `dev`/`main`/`master`, deleting that merged branch locally and on `origin`, plus orphaned directories older than the age threshold that a plain `git worktree remove` can no longer reach. It never removes an unmerged or in-flight worktree, and a reclaimed ticket's preserved WIP branch is unaffected because `--resume` fetches it from `origin` rather than from the local directory.

Running `harness close <TICKET> --run-id <id>` is allowed, including the Linear transition to Done and the merge and push of the run's own branch that the verb performs. The permission rides on the verb's gate rather than on trust: `close` refuses unless a `start` row exists for the same run, the worktree is clean, and a `verdict=pass` whose reviewed SHA equals the current HEAD is on record — refusing with `no_run`, `dirty_worktree`, `no_passing_review`, or `stale_review` otherwise. It can therefore only land work this run opened and a review already passed on, which is the same reviewed-work-only condition the `dev`-push clause above rests on.
